newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on profit-taking sales.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on profit-taking sales.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen futures contract on TIFFE ended slightly lower on Friday due to profit-taking sales, traders said.
An announcement by Tottori Bank that it would hold a news conference on its business activities in late afternoon had little effect on the market, traders said.
"Euroyen futures seemed a bit strong just before the news came out," a brokerage trader said.
A trader for a long-term credit bank said the announcement had little effect because it was soon followed by comments from a bank spokesman, who denied earlier market rumours about the bank.
Tottori Bank Ltd on Friday denied market rumours that it would merge with Sumitomo Bank Ltd or Sanwa Bank Ltd.
A bank spokesman said the bank president would hold a news conference in the late afternoon regarding its business activities.
The spokesman said the announcement would not cause worries about Japan's financial system.
Turnover of the June contract during Friday's day session was 24,189 contracts.
Turnover of the September contract in the day session was 36,860 contracts.
A benchmark shift will officially take place when the combined turnover of the day and night sessions for the September exceeds that of the June for two consecutive days.
Japan's key overnight call rate was most heavily traded at 0.48 percent by late afternoon, a trust bank trader said.
Friday's weighted average is likely to be 0.48 percent, which would be unchanged from Thursday, the trader said.
The Bank of Japan drained a net 900 billion yen from the money market this morning, maintaining its neutral stance.
About 20 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued on Friday at 0.50 percent.
About 10 billion yen worth of two-month CDs and 75 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were also issued.
All CD rates were unchanged from the previous day, at 0.50 percent.
